Summary: Adding a single item creates a cart row with the correct total cost
Cucumber Scenario:
Given an empty cart
When the shopper adds item EST-1 to the cart
Then the cart shows a row for item EST-1, product FI-SW-01, description "Large Angelfish", list price $16.50 and total cost $16.50

Summary: Adding an already-present item again increments its quantity instead of duplicating the row
Cucumber Scenario:
Given the cart already contains item EST-1 with quantity 1
When the shopper adds item EST-1 to the cart again
Then the EST-1 row's quantity becomes 2 and its total cost becomes $33.00
And no second EST-1 row is created
Description: condition: AC1-C2. low confidence — see open question in 02-understanding.md. assumption: Q1 -- adding an already-present item again increments its existing row's quantity and scales its total cost, rather than creating a duplicate row; not independently confirmed live (stateless fetch could not hold a session across two add calls).

Summary: The Sub Total equals the sum of every distinct item's total cost
Cucumber Scenario:
Given the cart already contains item EST-1 at $16.50 and item EST-2 at $16.50
When the shopper views the cart
Then the Sub Total equals $33.00

Summary: The Sub Total is displayed with two-decimal-place USD formatting
Cucumber Scenario:
Given the cart contains at least one item
When the shopper views the cart
Then the Sub Total is shown with exactly two decimal places
Description: condition: AC2-C4. low confidence — see open question in 02-understanding.md. assumption: Q6 -- Sub Total is displayed with standard two-decimal-place USD formatting; no source price forces a sub-cent rounding tie-break, so only the format invariant is asserted.

Summary: Cart contents persist after navigating away and back to the cart
Cucumber Scenario:
Given the shopper has added item EST-1 to the cart
When the shopper browses a different category and then returns to the cart
Then item EST-1 and its total cost $16.50 are still present
And the Sub Total is unchanged
Description: condition: AC2-C5. low confidence — see open question in 02-understanding.md. assumption: derived from istqb-design sub-step 3c (list-view state persistence) -- the cart is expected to persist across navigation within the same session; not independently confirmed.

Summary: Removing one item recomputes the Sub Total without affecting the remaining item
Cucumber Scenario:
Given the cart contains item EST-1 at $16.50 and item EST-2 at $16.50 with Sub Total $33.00
When the shopper removes the EST-1 row
Then the EST-1 row no longer appears in the cart
And the Sub Total decreases to $16.50

Summary: Checkout remains available with an out-of-stock item in the cart (proposed default, unconfirmed)
Cucumber Scenario:
Given the cart contains an item whose "In Stock?" value is false
When the shopper proceeds to checkout
Then the "Proceed to Checkout" action is available
Description: condition: AC3-C4. low confidence — see open question in 02-understanding.md. open: Q3 -- whether an item marked "In Stock? = false" blocks "Proceed to Checkout" is not confirmed by any source. Summary: A second, unrelated guest session cannot view or mutate the first session's cart (proposed default, unconfirmed)
Cucumber Scenario:
Given a shopper has added items to their own cart in session A
And a second, unrelated guest session B exists with no shared credential
When session B attempts to view or mutate session A's cart
Then the attempt is refused
And session A's cart is unaffected
Description: condition: AC3-C5. low confidence — see open question in 02-understanding.md. open: Q7 -- whether one guest session's cart is isolated from a second, unrelated guest session (no shared credential) is not confirmed by any source (stateless WebFetch could not hold two live sessions to compare). Proposed default generated below (refused/isolated): human arbitration required.
